title: Matrix-Vector Multiplication using OpenMP PARALLEL directive
question: To write a C program to compute the product y = A.x of an n x n matrix A and a vector x of length n, using the OpenMP PARALLEL directive to parallelize computation of the rows of the result.
whereToExecute: Linux terminal (Ubuntu / VM / WSL2), inside the lab working directory created during setup.
sampleOutput:
Thread 0 computed y[0] = 30 
Thread 2 computed y[2] = 110 
Thread 1 computed y[1] = 70 
Thread 3 computed y[3] = 150 
  
Resultant vector y = A.x : 
y[0] = 30 
y[1] = 70 
y[2] = 110 
y[3] = 150
note: Thread completion order may vary between runs since the four row computations execute concurrently; the final vector y is always identical.
result: The C program to write a C program to compute the product y = A.x of an n x n matrix A and a vector x of length n, using the OpenMP PARALLEL directive to parallelize computation of the rows of the result. was implemented and executed successfully, and the output was verified.

title: Parallel Supermarket Bill Processing using OpenMP Sections
question: A person purchases items across Clothing, Gaming, Grocery and Stationary sections. Write an OpenMP program to total each section's bill in parallel and display the final amount payable.
whereToExecute: Linux terminal (Ubuntu / VM / WSL2), inside the lab working directory created during setup.
sampleOutput:
Thread 1 -> Gaming total    = 4000.00 
Thread 0 -> Clothing total  = 2450.25 
Thread 2 -> Grocery total   = 306.50 
Thread 3 -> Stationary total= 75.50 
  
Final amount to be paid = 6832.25
note: Each #pragma omp section runs on a separate thread, so all four section totals are computed concurrently before being summed.
result: The C program to a person purchases items across Clothing, Gaming, Grocery and Stationary sections. Write an OpenMP program to total each section's bill in parallel and display the final amount payable. was implemented and executed successfully, and the output was verified.

title: Computing the value of Pi by Numerical Integration using OpenMP
question: To compute the value of Pi using the numerical integration (rectangle/mid-point rule) method, parallelized using OpenMP so that the summation is distributed across threads.
whereToExecute: Linux terminal (Ubuntu / VM / WSL2), inside the lab working directory created during setup.
sampleOutput:
Number of steps   = 100000 
Threads used      = 4 
Computed value of Pi = 3.1415926536 
Time taken         = 0.000842 seconds
note: The reduction(+:sum) clause gives every thread a private copy of sum which OpenMP automatically combines at the end of the parallel region, avoiding race conditions.
result: The C program to to compute the value of Pi using the numerical integration (rectangle/mid-point rule) method, parallelized using OpenMP so that the summation is distributed across threads. was implemented and executed successfully, and the output was verified.

title: Multi-threaded Fibonacci Series Generation and Printing (Producer-Consumer)
question: To design a multi-threaded OpenMP program to generate the Fibonacci series with one thread generating the numbers up to a specified limit and another thread printing them, using a lock for proper synchronization.
whereToExecute: Linux terminal (Ubuntu / VM / WSL2), inside the lab working directory created during setup.
sampleOutput:
[Generator - Thread 0] Generated fib[0] = 0 
        [Printer - Thread 1] Printed  fib[0] = 0 
[Generator - Thread 0] Generated fib[1] = 1 
        [Printer - Thread 1] Printed  fib[1] = 1 
[Generator - Thread 0] Generated fib[2] = 1 
        [Printer - Thread 1] Printed  fib[2] = 1 
[Generator - Thread 0] Generated fib[3] = 2 
        [Printer - Thread 1] Printed  fib[3] = 2 
[Generator - Thread 0] Generated fib[4] = 3 
        [Printer - Thread 1] Printed  fib[4] = 3 
... 
[Generator - Thread 0] Generated fib[9] = 34 
        [Printer - Thread 1] Printed  fib[9] = 34
note: The omp_lock_t guards the shared 'produced'/'consumed' counters and the fib[] array so the printer thread never reads a slot before the generator thread has written it. The exact interleaving of lines can vary run to run.
result: The C program to to design a multi-threaded OpenMP program to generate the Fibonacci series with one thread generating the numbers up to a specified limit and another thread printing them, using a lock for proper synchronization. was implemented and executed successfully, and the output was verified.

title: Total Mangoes Picked by N Robots using MPI
question: N robots each pick a number of mangoes from a farm in parallel; write an MPI program in which every process (robot) computes its own count and MPI_Reduce combines them into the total.
whereToExecute: Linux terminal (Ubuntu / VM / WSL2), inside the lab working directory created during setup.
sampleOutput:
Robot 2 picked 14 mangoes 
Robot 0 picked 7 mangoes 
Robot 3 picked 5 mangoes 
Robot 1 picked 19 mangoes 
  
Total mangoes picked by all 4 robots = 45
note: MPI_Reduce with MPI_SUM collects every process's local mangoes_picked value and sums them into 'total' on the root process (rank 0). Line order across robots may vary between runs.
result: The C program to n robots each pick a number of mangoes from a farm in parallel; write an MPI program in which every process (robot) computes its own count and MPI_Reduce combines them into the total. was implemented and executed successfully, and the output was verified.

title: MPI Program using Blocking and Non-Blocking Send/Receive
question: To design an MPI program that demonstrates both blocking (MPI_Send/MPI_Recv) and non-blocking (MPI_Isend/MPI_Irecv with MPI_Wait) point-to-point communication between two processes.
whereToExecute: Linux terminal (Ubuntu / VM / WSL2), inside the lab working directory created during setup.
sampleOutput:
Process 0: sent 100 using BLOCKING send 
Process 1: received 100 using BLOCKING receive 
Process 0: sent 200 using NON-BLOCKING send 
Process 1: received 200 using NON-BLOCKING receive
note: MPI_Send/MPI_Recv block until the message transfer is complete; MPI_Isend/MPI_Irecv return immediately and the transfer is confirmed later using MPI_Wait, allowing computation to overlap with communication.

title: MPI Collective Communication (Broadcast, Scatter, Gather, Reduce)
question: To design an MPI program that demonstrates the application of collective communication routines: MPI_Bcast, MPI_Scatter, MPI_Gather and MPI_Reduce.
whereToExecute: Linux terminal (Ubuntu / VM / WSL2), inside the lab working directory created during setup.
sampleOutput:
Process 0 received broadcast data = 55 
Process 1 received broadcast data = 55 
Process 2 received broadcast data = 55 
Process 3 received broadcast data = 55 
Process 0 received scattered value = 10 
Process 1 received scattered value = 20 
Process 2 received scattered value = 30 
Process 3 received scattered value = 40 
Process 0 gathered values : 100 200 300 400 
Process 0: sum of all values (Reduce) = 1000
note: This program must be run with exactly -np 4 because scatter_data[] and the sample output assume 4 processes. MPI_Bcast copies data to every process, MPI_Scatter distributes distinct chunks, MPI_Gather collects them back, and MPI_Reduce combines them with an operator (here, SUM).
result: The C program to to design an MPI program that demonstrates the application of collective communication routines: MPI_Bcast, MPI_Scatter, MPI_Gather and MPI_Reduce. was implemented and executed successfully, and the output was verified.
